difficulty_why: Developers can immediately activate Public Distribution for direct OAuth installs, but commercial broad distribution and avoiding Tier 1 rate throttling on conversation history requires Slack Marketplace review taking up to 10-12 weeks.

dev_time.label: 15-30 min
dev_time.text: Time to create an app in the Slack API console, configure redirect URLs, add scopes, enable public distribution, and retrieve client credentials.

launch_time.label: 10-12 weeks
launch_time.text: While unlisted public distribution enables immediate direct OAuth installs for pilots, commercial distribution without Tier 1 rate throttling requires Slack Marketplace review (up to 10 business days preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks functional review, requiring 5-10 active test workspaces first).

app_type.label: Slack App (OAuth 2.0 v2)
app_type.text: Slack App using OAuth 2.0 v2 with granular bot and user scopes, configured with Public Distribution enabled to allow multi-workspace authorization.

prerequisites.label: Slack account and workspace
prerequisites.text: A Slack account with permissions to install and create applications in a development workspace.

prerequisites.label: No paid plan or partner program required
prerequisites.text: Creating a Slack app and activating unlisted public distribution does not require a paid Slack subscription or partner program membership.

prerequisites.label: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.text: A secure HTTPS redirect URL endpoint to receive authorization callback requests.

prerequisites.label: Distribution checklist completion
prerequisites.text: Completing Slack's distribution checklist in Manage Distribution (redirect URL, scopes, and app details) before activating public distribution.

steps.label: Create Slack App
steps.text: Go to the Slack API console at https://api.slack.com/apps, click 'Create New App', choose 'From scratch', specify an App Name, and select your development workspace.

fields.label: Pick a workspace to develop your app in

steps.label: Configure redirect URL
steps.text: In your app settings sidebar, select 'OAuth & Permissions', scroll down to 'Redirect URLs', click 'Add New Redirect URL', enter the redirect URI, and click 'Save URLs'.

steps.label: Add OAuth scopes
steps.text: On the 'OAuth & Permissions' page, scroll down to 'Scopes' and add the required scopes under Bot Token Scopes or User Token Scopes.

steps.label: Activate public distribution
steps.text: In the sidebar under Settings, navigate to 'Manage Distribution', verify the prerequisite checklist items under 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces', and click 'Activate Public Distribution'.

steps.label: Retrieve credentials
steps.text: In the sidebar under Settings, click 'Basic Information', scroll down to 'App Credentials', and copy the 'Client ID' and 'Client Secret'.

scopes.label: search:read and search:read.*
scopes.text: Explicitly flagged as restricted/unsuitable for Slack Marketplace apps; broad search scopes require special partner justification.

scopes.label: channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history
scopes.text: Reviewed strictly under least privilege; banned for message archiving or LLM training; commercial unlisted apps are throttled to Tier 1 (1 req/min).

scopes.label: chat:write
scopes.text: Standard message posting scope usable across workspaces immediately once Public Distribution is enabled.

scopes.label: users:read and users:read.email
scopes.text: Basic identity discovery scopes available immediately for unlisted public distribution without prior review.

scopes.label: files:read and files:write
scopes.text: Standard file interaction scopes operational immediately upon public distribution activation.

scopes.label: reactions:read and reactions:write
scopes.text: Standard reaction scopes available immediately without advance approval.

approval.label: When required
approval.text: Marketplace review is not technically required to share an OAuth install link across workspaces once Public Distribution is turned on; however, Slack's API Terms of Service mandate Marketplace listing for commercial distribution.

approval.label: What's checked
approval.text: Slack performs a preliminary review of metadata and installation flow, followed by a functional review evaluating security, user experience, privacy, and least privilege scope usage.

approval.label: Wait
approval.text: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days for feedback, and functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new app submissions.

approval.label: Cost
approval.text: Slack does not charge any fee for Slack Marketplace review or listing ($0).

approval.label: Common rejections
approval.text: Rejections stem from requesting restricted scopes such as search:read, bulk message scraping, using Slack data to train LLMs, or failing the 5-10 active workspace minimum.

approval.label: Before approval
approval.text: Apps must be fully functioning and installed on at least 5 to 10 active workspaces with 10 weekly active users before submitting to the Marketplace.

approval.label: Install cap before review
approval.text: Slack does not enforce a numerical maximum cap on workspace installs for unlisted apps with Public Distribution activated.

approval.label: Limits until reviewed
approval.text: Commercial apps distributed outside the Slack Marketplace are throttled to Tier 1 rate limits (1 request per minute, max 15 messages) on conversations.history and conversations.replies.

pitfalls.label: Restricted search scopes
pitfalls.text: Requesting search:read or search:read.* is explicitly flagged as unsuitable/restricted in Marketplace guidelines and will cause rejection unless authorized under partner access.

pitfalls.label: Commercial unlisted rate throttling
pitfalls.text: Commercially distributing an unlisted app outside the Marketplace triggers strict Tier 1 rate limits (1 req/min, max 15 messages) on conversations.history and conversations.replies for all new installs.

pitfalls.label: Prerequisite active workspace minimum
pitfalls.text: Developers cannot submit an unreviewed app for Marketplace approval until it is already installed and tested on 5 to 10 active workspaces used within the past 28 days.

pitfalls.label: Redirect URI mismatch
pitfalls.text: The redirect_uri sent during authorization and token exchange must match a registered Redirect URL exactly, or Slack returns a bad_redirect_uri error.

pitfalls.label: HTTPS requirement
pitfalls.text: Slack requires all OAuth redirect URLs to use HTTPS and prohibits HTTP URLs and URLs containing anchor fragments.

pitfalls.label: Scope updates require reinstall
pitfalls.text: Adding or modifying scopes in app settings does not update existing tokens; previously authorized workspaces must re-authorize the app before new permissions take effect.

email_subject: Inquiry regarding Slack OAuth app review, scope policies, and commercial distribution for [Your Product Name]
email_body:
Hi Slack Platform Support Team,

We are developing an AI agent platform ([Your Product Name]) that integrates with Slack via OAuth 2.0 using granular scopes so our users can connect their Slack workspaces.

We plan to use the following OAuth scopes:
- Messaging & Content: chat:write, files:read, files:write, reactions:read, reactions:write, pins:read, pins:write, links:read, links:write
- Channel & Message History: channels:read, channels:history, groups:read, groups:history, im:read, im:history, mpim:read, mpim:history
- Users & Teams: users:read, users:read.email, users.profile:read, users.profile:write, team:read, usergroups:read
- Search & Additional: search:read, search:read.public, search:read.private, search:read.files, reminders:read, reminders:write, dnd:read, dnd:write

Could you please clarify:
1. Since search:read and message history scopes are heavily scrutinized in Marketplace review, what documentation or architectural safeguards are required for an AI agent tool assisting individual workspace users?
2. Are unlisted apps with Public Distribution enabled permitted for commercial SaaS customer rollouts during the Marketplace review period, or will new installs be strictly throttled to Tier 1 on conversations.history?
3. What is the current turnaround time for preliminary and functional reviews for new apps?

Best regards,
[Your Name]
